question.worked_solution:
We need to isolate $u,$ so we will treat the other variables $t$ and $q$ as constants. We can use the addition and multiplication principles to solve for $u.$

First, we add $t$ from both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{ut}{3}-t & =2q \\ \frac{ut}{3}-t+t & =2q+t \\ \frac{ut}{3} & =2q+t\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we multiply by $3$ to get rid of the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{ut}{3} & =2q+t \\ 3\cdot \frac{ut}{3} & =3\cdot (2q+t) \\ ut & =3(2q+t)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide by $t$ to get $u$ alone:

$$
\begin{aligned}ut & =3(2q+t) \\ \frac{ut}{t} & =\frac{3(2q+t)}{t} \\ u & =\frac{3(2q+t)}{t}\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** This result assumes that $t\ne 0.$
